title.narrative: Ebola virus disease response in eastern DRC (BOAD) (Bundibugyo virus)

description.narrative:
The Ebola virus disease (EVD) outbreak declared in mid-May 2026 in the Democratic Republic of Congo has rapidly escalated into a major public health emergency. As of 24–25 May 2026, more than 900 suspected cases and around 101 confirmed cases have been reported, with at least 119 suspected deaths and 10 confirmed deaths, and overall figures approaching or exceeding 1,000 total cases. The outbreak is primarily concentrated in Ituri Province, with confirmed spread to North and South Kivu, including key urban centres such as Bunia and Goma, heightening the risk of wider transmission in densely populated and highly mobile areas. Cross-border spread has already been reported, with confirmed cases in Uganda, indicating growing regional implications.
The situation is unfolding in a highly complex humanitarian and security environment, which is significantly amplifying transmission risks. Key drivers include ongoing armed conflict, population displacement, attacks on health facilities, and low levels of trust between communities and response actors. In addition, limited contact tracing capacity, challenges in enforcing safe burial practices, and the absence of an approved vaccine for the current strain are hindering containment efforts. As a result, the outbreak shows early signs of sustained community transmission and continued geographic spread, making it operationally difficult to control.
In response, national authorities, WHO, Africa CDC, and international partners are scaling up surveillance, case management, and emergency response measures, including deployment of rapid response teams, strengthening screening, and imposing public health restrictions. However, critical gaps remain in health system capacity, community engagement, infection prevention, and access to affected populations, particularly in insecure areas.
Within this context, BOAD proposes a targeted, integrated response in North Kivu, focusing on community engagement, WASH interventions, and support to frontline health services. Priority actions include risk communication and awareness campaigns to improve community acceptance, distribution of hygiene kits and installation of handwashing facilities, and provision of essential supplies and training to health workers. This approach aims to contain transmission at community level, reduce infection risks, and support the broader coordinated response, while ensuring alignment with government and humanitarian strategies.
